title: Your prompt sucks: prepare a reference, blueprint and success brief before you prompt
summary: Ruben argues that asking ChatGPT to write your prompt gives vague results, because prompting is thinking, not typing. His method: find a reference and convert it to markdown, reverse-engineer it into a short blueprint, write a 4-question success brief, then stack all three into one prompt and keep chatting to steer toward the result.

principles.text: Prompting is thinking, not typing: prepare before you write a single word.
principles.quote: Most people think prompting = typing. But prompting = thinking.

principles.text: Asking AI to write your prompt fails: vague descriptions, no definition of success, everything in one shot.
Match effort to stakes: quick lookups need no complex prompt, serious tasks need a specific method.
principles.quote: You do NOT need to use a complex prompt for this.

principles.text: Start from a concrete reference converted to markdown, then reverse-engineer it into a short blueprint.
principles.quote: Analyze this reference so you can recreate something similar later.

principles.text: Write a success brief with four answers: output type and length, recipient reaction, what it must not sound like, and what success means.
principles.quote: Does NOT sound like**: \[What to avoid — generic AI, too casual, too legal, jargon-heavy?\]

principles.text: Treat AI as a conversation: correct errors immediately, keep messages short, steer toward convergence, and reset a bloated chat.
